snippet.title: How much do web designers earn? [My salary history]
snippet.description:
Revealing all the different salaries I've had throughout my career! It's a little scary to talk about money in this way, but I wanted to be open about this because although salaries are relative to your experience, where you live, what size company you work for etc, I think you'll get value from hearing about my progression and what has led to my salary increases over my 8 year career so far. So if you've been wondering what designers earn, this video is my perspective on the matter!

snippet.title: Designing & building my blog! | Episode 4 of Designing a Website
snippet.description:
Hear about the design and build process for my new blog, as well as see some fun interactions I built for it! In this video you'll get a look at my design file and the iterations I tried, and see how I've set up the Webflow CMS for my blog.

My goals for designing the blog was for it to be a good reading experience first and foremost! I didn't want every post to rely on having a fancy feature image, and I wanted it to be super easy for me to add a new post to (so that I'd have less excuses not to publish...) Take a look at the blog design on my live site and let me know what you think! https://charlimarie.com/blog

I'd highly recommend watching this in full screen so you can better see all my settings in Webflow, although I tried to zoom in on the important stuff. 


** Try Webflow out for yourself: http://bit.ly/cmwebflow **
(affiliate link)

and watch the full playlist of website redesign: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLrJQSKQvgHS6BCO8nZScJ9iw7Ukjv4f9C

snippet.title: 5 common Webflow mistakes (& how to avoid them!)

Looking back at my first ever Webflow project and at others' first Webflow builds I noticed a few common mistakes that I wanted to highlight and show you how to avoid! Your future self will thank you for changing these habits and building Webflow sites in a more efficient way.

Huge thanks to Webflow for sponsoring this video and continuing to support my channel!

snippet.title: Improve your designs with ITERATION
snippet.description:
Your first idea is never your best. Iteration will make you a better designer! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

In this video I demonstrate the iteration/design process with a graphic to advertise a workshop, but I go through this same iteration process when I design websites. I hope this video answers questions about why you should 'bother' to design first before you code, and I hope it encourages you to really push your ideas further. Don't settle for the first thing you create! You can always find small ways to improve it. 

A side note that i didn't cover in the video, is you also need to know when to end the iteration process. I could have kept going for days trying different things with this graphic, but there was other work to do! So another part of iterating is learning when to stop; when to call it 'done' and move on to the next project!

snippet.title: How to earn more for your design work! (with Chris Do)
snippet.description:
Chris and I are both passionate about designers being paid what they're worth. Watch for lots of advice about how to increase your rates and price your work based on value! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Check out Chris's channel, The Futur, for lots more actionable and amazingly useful design business advice: http://youtube.com/thefuturishere

Designer's often struggle to price themselves fairly and be paid what they're worth. In this video we talk about the importance of learning how to price your work, and cover the three pricing models you can use: pricing based on time and materials, based on a fixed project fee, or based on the value the client will receive from you solving their problem. The last model is the most lucrative, and the hardest to get into! Chris shares lots of great advice for how to price this way and what to ask the client to uncover the value. I bet you'll finish this video feeling super empowered and ready to increase your rates and be paid more for your work!

We filmed this video together during Epicurrence, a conference for creatives that was held in Yosemite. It was snowing and we were sitting outside by a fire!

snippet.title: Simple Bullet Journal Setup 2018
snippet.description:
Take a look at the set up of my 2018 bullet journal, designed purely for productivity and organisation! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

There are many beautiful, creative, artsy bullet journals out there; this is not one of them! I started using the bullet journal last year and found it SO useful for staying organised. I don't draw in it or get creative, it's purely functional. Hopefully you enjoy watching as I set up all the spreads I need for 2018 and see how easy and simple a bullet journal can be (and that you really don't need to be super creative, or have nice hand writing for it to be useful!).

If you use the bullet journal system, or if you tried it but it didn't work for you, tell me about it in the comments!

// LINKS

My 2017 bullet journal video: https://youtu.be/inlYt5RsPYU

Designers need to stop complaining about 'clients from hell'. snippet.title: A chat about feeling unsuccessful - day three | Charli Marie in NYC
snippet.description:
A super chatty vlog about success and feeling down about yourself. Plus working remotely in NYC! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Probably not what you were expecting for the day three in NYC vlog, but I hope you enjoy listening to this chat. I woke up just feeling a bit low and like I hadn't made a good impression on people at the meetup the previous night because I didn't talk about my projects or come across very interesting. Then I tweeted about it and realised hundreds of other people feel this way too sometimes! if you're feeling like that right now, or even if you're in a good space at the moment, I want you to write something you're proud of in the comments. Give yourself a break and recognise your achievements. It's okay that you feel like you've not achieved everything yet. That just means you have big goals! But you need to recognise the work you've done to this point. So, something little, something big, whatever it is tell me about it in the comments!

I promise I will actually show you Manhattan tomorrow.

snippet.title: Bullet journal flip through - My basic setup for managing tasks & goals
snippet.description:
Take a tour through my bullet journal and hear about why I use this analogue task management system! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I was definitely late to the bullet journal band wagon, but I decided to dive in and start trying it out because I'd heard great things about it from others, and figured it could be fun to try. Turns out I LOVE it and have pretty much stopped using to do list apps as a result!

My bullet journal is not filled with creative, beautiful, colorful spreads. It's very plain and definitely focusses on function. I knew if I tried to make it super arty I would feel imposter syndrome with it and be scared to put pen to paper, so instead I've embraced my messy handwriting and lack of drawing abilities and come up with a way of organising my notebook that's highly functional and helps me keep track of all my tasks and projects and work towards my goals. 

Hope you enjoy seeing it! tell me about your own bullet journal in the comments, and if you don't have one yet, here's what I use:

Leuchtrum bullet journal: http://amzn.to/2ntGEnv
Muji 0.7 black gel pen: http://www.muji.eu/pages/online.asp?Sec=13&Sub=52&PID=5163
Metal ruler: http://amzn.to/2nHh8ME

snippet.title: My experience as a female designer in tech
snippet.description:
Some thoughts on how working in a male-dominated industry has influenced my design style and experience. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

As a very proud feminist, I thought it was about time I talked about gender diversity in the tech design industry. Since I started working in tech I noticed that this sector of the design industry is dominated by white males, and that's had an influence on the way I work and the way I view 'professional' design. I'm not sure I explained it properly in this video but hopefully you get the point I was attempting to make and can understand what I mean. I definitely want to hear your thoughts so please share them in the comments. Whether you're male, female or non-binary, what have you noticed about gender diversity in design? 

Let's keep the comments constructive! I'll be deleting any from trolls or that simply add negativity to the conversation.

Things get nerdy today as we chat about why it's important for the image assets you're building in to a website (or passing on to a developer to use) should be as small as possible without compromising on quality. In this video I show you some best practices for exporting three different file types: .svg, .png and .jpg, and I also walk you through when it's best to use each one.

I'm a marketing designer! Let me tell you what that means and what it takes to be good at it. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Marketing design is not a job I ever heard of until I stumbled across a job listing one day when a friend was referring me for a design job at a tech company. It turns out, it's the perfect job for me! In this video I explain what it means to be a marketing designer and the skills and traits it takes to do a good job. I hope you enjoy it! And I hope you can tell from the way I talk about it that I really do love what I do.

Please feel free to ask questions in the comments!


If you're a graphic designer and you like the sound of this job, check out this video for some help with making the transition.

Moving from print to web design: https://youtu.be/4GA1wp9jpkA

snippet.title: The Six Stages of the Creative Process | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
The stages every creative goes through with each project. Shot on the green screen at YouTube Space London as part of YouTube NextUp 2016. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I was chosen as a winner of YouTube NextUp earlier this year and got to spend a week learning lots about production and content strategy at the London YouTube space. As part of our production challenge, we had to film a video that took us out of our comfort zone so I decided to create something using the green screen! This video is inspired by a poster that hangs in my room which was designed by my pal Dan Edwards: https://dribbble.com/shots/1826840--lunchtimedrawings-The-Creative-Process

I don't know about you, but pretty much every project I work on goes through this emotional rollercoaster, so I wrote a little thing to express it, and then attempted some acting. Please give it a thumbs up if you enjoy it and let me know what you think in the comments! I know it's not my usual style of video but I'm really proud of it.

Thanks for letting me use your art as inspiration Dan! Follow him here: http://twitter.com/de

Huge thank you to our NextUp mentor Phil for helping us film and teaching us so much.

And thanks to my group-mates for handing me pieces of paper and helping me get the shot!

snippet.title: Speaking at seanwes conference - Austin, Texas 2016 part 2 | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
I gave a talk at seanwes conference in Austin, Texas! Here's a vlog of my time at the conference. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I was so honoured to be invited to speak at the first ever seanwes conference. It was a life-altering experience, and not just because I was speaking! The people at the conference were absolutely amazing and I had so many valuable conversations there, and made so many new friends. As you can see at some points in this video, it was all a bit overwhelming at times, but in the best possible way. I hope this video captures how awesome the experience was in some way! I'll be going back next year as an attendee :)

My talk was 45 mins long, so while I won't be recording it to put up on YouTube, I am going to be making videos with sections of it! Stay tuned for the first one, on time management coming out this weekend.

snippet.title: Album artwork design critique | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:

snippet.title: Web design & web development - What's the difference? | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
There is often confusion around what exactly web design and development are and that they're two separate roles. Find out why in this video! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Not all web designers know how to build the sites they design, and not all web developers know how to design sites well in order to build them; and that's okay! While some people are able to do both, they are different skillsets, and each is a perfectly valid and important role on its own. I hope this video helps to demystify the difference between them, and explains why it's okay to focus only on one. 

Want more on this topic? Check out this episode of my podcast, it's titled 'Should designer's learn to code': http://designlife.fm/episode25/

snippet.title: Design Inspiration & Copying | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Talking about how to be inspired by other people's work without copying it... Please remember to subscribe! http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Copying other peoples work to learn from is okay, as long as you don't share it or try to pass it off as your own. But the best way to be inspired by other peoples work is not to copy it directly, but to be influenced by certain pieces of it, and mix it with inspiration from other pieces to create something new. snippet.title: Designer's Guide to Stock Photography | sponsored by GraphicStock | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:

Get a free 7 day trial of their site here: http://graphicstock.com/x/CharliMarieTV_0616

--

Stock images can help make your design process faster and save you money on setting up shoots yourself when you just need a quick photo to set the scene of your content online, or to use in the background of a graphic. They've got a reputation for being cheesy, but as with most things, it comes down to choosing the right image to use. Hope you enjoy hearing my advice about when is best to take advantage of using them, and how to pick out the best ones! What do you think about stock photography? I went to Amsterdam for TNW conference and had 3.5 lovely days of friends, inspiration, cycling and cuddles with an adorable cat. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

Hope you enjoy this travel vlog! I was there for a conference rather than sight-seeing, but still got to cycle around the city and see lots of pretty canals. I love Amsterdam! Mostly though I loved hanging out with two of my best friends, and cuddling their adorable cat. Thumbs up this video for my vlogging while cycling? (Don't worry Mum there was no traffic around)

The conference was great! So well organised and had sooo many talks from inspiring people including my all time fave YouTuber Casey Neistat, and from hustler extraordinaire Gary Vee. Read my blog post with my top insights from TNW here: https://charlimarie.com/2016/06/02/insights-from-tnw-conference

Watch the replay of the Design Life livestream: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDXn9EM4EZc#t=10

snippet.title: What client feedback REALLY means - Part two | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Deciphering common pieces of client feedback and giving you advice for dealing with it! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

We can't expect our freelance clients to give us super detailed, useful feedback. They're not design professionals who know how to critique work; we are! It's our job as designers to ask further questions and explain things to them when we get vague and annoying feedback. This helps us work out what they really mean, and makes for a better working relationship! And as a bonus, hopefully the client will learn some new ways to talk about design for next time. 

Hope you enjoyed seeing part two in this series! Watch part one below, and if you want to see a part three, leave some feedback suggestions in the comments!

What clients really mean, part one: https://youtu.be/vNL4PS1KCHY

snippet.title: DIY Customised Denim Jacket | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Get tips for customising your own denim jacket, and see how I made mine! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I'd been wanting to make myself a 'signature' item of clothing that I own for years and is super unique to me; that's where this denim jacket comes in! In this DIY project I customised it to represent some pieces of my personality and my style and I LOVE how it turned out! I'll keep adding little bits and pieces to it over the years as I find stuff I love, but this is a great base for now, and I've worn it nearly every day since I made it (as you will have seen in my vlogs). 

If you were to customise a jacket, what pieces of your personality would you make sure were represented?

snippet.title: Weekly vlog: What I do to avoid burnout | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
A busy week of work and side projects and what i do to stop tiredness getting the best of me! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT


The key to avoiding burnout is noticing the warning signs! I felt SO tired and exhausted at the start of the week and feared I was heading towards getting sick or burning out, so I adapted my routine to give myself time to get better and catch up on sleep! I still got stuff, done, but not as much as I would have normally. Hope you enjoy seeing my week!

snippet.title: What client feedback REALLY means | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Clients sometimes give us designers super vague feedback... here's how to decipher it and work out what they REALLY mean! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

We can't expect our freelance clients to give us super detailed, useful feedback. They're not design professionals who know how to critique work; we are! It's our job as designers to ask further questions and explain things to them when we get vague and annoying feedback. This helps us work out what they really mean, and makes for a better working relationship! And as a bonus, hopefully the client will learn some new ways to talk about design for next time. 

Hope you enjoy me dissecting these pieces of common feedback. let me know if you want a part two of this video, and feel free to share any vague advice you've received in the comments!

Research into the myth of 'the fold' in web design: 
http://iampaddy.com/lifebelow600/
http://rareview.com/scrolling-and-the-above-the-fold-myth/

In the last year of most design degrees you'll do a final research or thesis project that will involve researching a topic and then creating something from that research that relates to the topic and solves a problem you've investigated. snippet.title: Ikea Hack: DIY Standing Desk  | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Here's the pieces of Ikea furniture I've put together to make my own standing desk! I'll give you tips for making your own too. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I fell in love with working at a standing desk when my office back in New Zealand got some fancy electronic ones that could easily move from a sitting to a standing position. Unfortunately, those are expensive! So finally I've worked out an 'Ikea hack' to put together a few pieces of furniture to make a DIY standing desk setup that works for both me and my much-taller boyfriend. 

To make your own standing desk measure from the ground to just below your elbow, and then play the game of finding furniture that when put together make that height. My setup is not adjustable but if you are also 170cm tall (or a bit taller) this one might work well for you too! My pieces are linked below.

snippet.title: New podcast! Design Life trailer | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
I'm excited to announce my new podcast with my friend and fellow designer, Femke, launches today! Check it out at http://designlife.fm

Subscribe in iTunes and leave us a rating to help us out! https://itunes.apple.com/gb/podcast/design-life/id1063264363?mt=2

Follow Femke on Twitter: http://www.twitter.com/femkesvs
Check out her work: http://theapartment.co

Design Life is a podcast about design and side projects for motivated creators. It was born after your hosts, two serial side project addicts, saw a gap in the podcast market for a conversational show about design and the issues young creatives face, that was hosted by two females.

This show aims to tackle the big issues designers face like getting paid, overcoming a creative block or managing time, to name a few. We want to open up discussion about things we wish we heard people talk about when we were studying, and we want to chat to you about the joys and the frustrations of working in the tech industry by day, and on our passion projects in the rest of our waking hours. We hope that by doing so, Design Life will give you a dose of motivation or inspiration when you need it.

New episodes will launch every Monday morning, and you can check the first two out here: http://designlife.fm

We're so excited to see what you think about the show!

snippet.title: How to screen print t-shirts at home (DIY method) | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
An in-depth explanation of how to screen print your own t-shirts talking through how to expose your screens, and how to use them. Get the PDF guide when you submit your email on this page: http://www.charlimarie.com/screen-printing

Links to all the tools & equipment used for DIY screen printing: https://charlimarie.com/screen-printing#tools

This is a long video for a reason! There is a lot involved with the DIY screen printing process and I've tried to explain it step by step as well as possible. Hopefully this video will be a great resource for anyone wanting to start their own t-shirt company, print t-shirts for fun, or even just learn more about how the screen printing process works. 

I've created a screen-printing guide to go along with this video that gives you clearly written, step-by-step instructions for how to go about making your own frames, exposing your screen, and printing your t-shirt. Submit your email address in the form on the page linked at the top of the description box!

snippet.title: Weekly vlog #27: YouTube Halloween party & Oxford St Christmas lights! | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
A week of festive-ness heading along to the YouTube Space Halloween party, and seeing the Oxford St Christmas lights turned on! Oh, and a gig and some work as well. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

A busy week as per usual! So busy in fact that now I am sick :( Maybe there was something in that fog you'll see at the end... This week was fun though! Mark and I went to see Our Last Night play with Palisades and Crooks, I worked from home for two days on a big project, then went to the YouTube Space London Halloween party with Lu and Sandra and met some new friends, yay for new friends! I got a lot of filming and other stuff done on Sunday, and went to see the Christmas lights turned on on Oxford St! Surely it's way too early for that no? But fun to get into the festive spirit early. I plan on fully embracing the Christmas spirit this year as there just seems to be an abundance of it in England! 

How was your week? What did you dress up as for Halloween??

snippet.title: Week Vlog #26: Warped Tour & Back To The Future | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
A weekend filled with concerts then a mid-week screening of Back to The Future, plus filing, working and scary footage of me with no makeup. Follow my London life  by subscribing! http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I've been feeling lately like I'm not making the most of London and all it has to offer. But then I watch vlogs like this as I edit them and realise I actually fill my life to the brim! In this vlog I go to a Fightstar gig, and then to Warped Tour UK, then to some films, a tech meetup and a day shooting at some beautiful London locations with my friend Matt. snippet.title: How to wireframe a website | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Wireframing is the first stage of the web design process, and in this video I show you how I do it and give you some advice! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

If you've ever wondered how to wireframe a website, or if you want to know how to design a website and you've never heard of wireframing, this video is dedicated to you! Yes, you. Wireframing is the process of laying out the bones or the structure of a website to think about how the information will be organised on the page before you start thinking about colours and fonts and other visual things. Using the wireframe process I teach you in this video you'll be able to generate lots of ideas for different ways to arrange your website and be able to decide on the best one from there.

I hope you enjoy the video! Please make sure you give it a thumbs up if you do. I'm still learning how to make tutorials MY way (not just screen casts) so any feedback is much appreciated. I ant these videos to feel like we're sitting in a room together and I'm showing you what to do, rather than you just looking at my screen as I do something. Does that make sense? 

If there's something design-related you're struggling with that you'd like a tutorial on next, let me know!

snippet.title: Saving vs splurging: My advice for spending on fashion | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
I love making sure I spend my money wisely, so in this video I tell you about what items I try to buy cheaply and which I don't mind splurging on. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

I want to say first off that what cost is associated with 'cheap' or 'expensive' clothes for me will probably be totally different to what cost is associated with those things for other people, and that is 100% okay! This video isn't about the exact cost of items (though I have included them as examples so you can see what my deal is) but rather about what kinds of items I think are worth spending more on than others, whatever your budget may be. :)

I wish that I could have lots of lovely good quality clothes but unfortunately there are pesky things called bills to pay that soak up most of my paycheck, so when I invest in a fashion item, you best believe I want to be really sure of my decision as I would hate for it to be a waste! I used to only buy cheap clothes because I was scared of wasting my money, but now I'm in the mindset that there are some things that are okay to splash out a little on. I wanted to share that with you today in case you've been wanting to invest a little more in your wardrobe but want to make sure it's worth it.

Let's not talk dollars and cents (or pounds or euros or whatever), but I'd love to hear what kinds of clothing and accessory items you guys find worthy of spending more on, and what your fashion budget buys are, so please let me know down below in the comments! That way we can all get ideas from each other :)

snippet.title: What is design? More than 'making things pretty' | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
This week I have a design chat video for you with a bit of a rant on why design is more than just making things look pretty. Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

What is design? What does a designer actually do? I passionately believe that design should be seen as an academic subject in schools and it should be seen as a smart career choice. I hope this video will explain why! Being a designer is such a great job because it involves equal parts creativity and critical thinking/problem solving, so there's rarely a dull moment. 

If you're a designer, please weigh in with your thoughts in the comments. And if you're not a designer, I'd love to know if this video sort of makes you see design in a new light! 

Let me know too if you liked this sort of video, or what you'd like to see in future design videos :)

snippet.title: Weekly Vlog #11: Valencia Fallas festival | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
This week I went on a trip to Valencia Spain to see my boyfriend and the Fallas festival! Please remember to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT

When I first went to Valencia in 2009 I just so happened to be there at the right time for Fallas, and I've wanted to go again ever since so I'm pleased I got to this year in 2015! As with many things in Spain it's a traditional religious festival, but really it's about community spirit and creativity. (EDIT: thanks to a lovely commenter for letting me know that wikipedia is wrong, its not a religious festival, it just has religious elements) Each little community creates a Falla (giant sculpture made from wood+ papier-mache) that is often a satirical commentary or something relevant to the community. There's a competition for the best one, and on the last night of Fallas every Falla except the winning one is stuffed with fireworks and burned in something called la crema! There are also fireworks displays and macletas (sound fireworks) throughout the weeks and it's basically just awesome. here's some links to read more about it:

http://www.valenciavalencia.com/culture-guide/fallas/about-fallas.htm
http://www.visitvalencia.com/en/whats-on-offer-valencia/festivities/the-fallas

Check out the store here: http://linernotekids.storenvy.com/

This video was requested a while ago and since I just released a new line of t-shirts for my little t-shirt business I thought it was the perfect time to talk about how I design t-shirts. I often get questions about what software I use, but I honestly believe that design isn't about the software you use to create something. Design is a skill and software is just a tool for creating, there isn't some magical t-shirt design software that will do the creative job for you unfortunately!

As you'll see in the video I do a lot of hand drawn stuff for my tshirts. but if you're really interested in the software, I vectorise the drawings in Illustrator and sometimes just tweak the contrast in Photoshop if my scanned drawing is high-res.

If there's anything else you're curious about let me know! I love talking about design so would love to answer any questions :)

snippet.title: Earring organiser DIY Christmas present idea | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
Christmas is coming! Why not try hand making some gifts this year? Check out this DIY for some Earring organiser frames in this collaboration with ShopStyleConquer. Please click to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT and OPEN for all the juicy details...

Giving great presents at Christmas time doesn't always mean spending a lot of money. Myself and two of my favourite girls on YouTube, Tara and Ellen of ShopStyleConquer (https://www.youtube.com/user/shopstyleconquer) have collabed to give you a couple of homemade gift ideas! We decided to keep it a secret what we were making, then sent each other the DIYs as a gift to open on camera!

Tara and Ellen made some absolutely gorgeous and special looking bath bombs and bath treats. Go check out their video on how to make them here: http://youtu.be/Gj9NlYru7ug

// THE QUESTIONS

1. You have to get rid of all your foundations and you can only keep one high end and one drugstore, which do you keep?

2. You go for an interview and the lady interviewing you has lipstick on her teeth. Do you approach the subject or ignore it completely?

3. You're not feeling yourself and need a pick me up. Which lipstick do you put on to make yourself feel beautiful?

4. You go back in time for a day to your teenage years, how would you do your hair and makeup differently?

5. You ask your hairdresser for a shoulder length Pixie Lott hair cut, but they hear wrong and give you a pixi cut. Do you a) Smile, say thank you, leave and call your mum hysterical b) Cry in the chair and things get awkward or c) Complain to the manager and demand a refund.

6. Your friend surprises you with a 4 day city break and you have 1 hour to pack. Which 'do it all' palette do you pack in your makeup bag?

7. Your house has been robbed, don't worry everyone is safe, but your beauty stash has been raided. What's the product you really hope is safe?

8. Your friend borrows your makeup and returns it in awful condition. Do you a) Just pretend you haven't noticed b) Ask them to repurchase it or c) Secretly do the same to something of theirs

snippet.title: Design chat: Should you work for free? | CharliMarieTV
snippet.description:
This week I tackle something I feel very passionate about, designers being asked to do work for free. have a listen to my opinion then share yours in the comments! Please click to subscribe http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT and OPEN for more info...

I'm not entirely sure I explained everything correctly in this video as this is definitely a trick topic with a lot of grey areas. However, the gist of it is I do not think young designers (or designers of any age or place in their career) should be expected to do work for free under the guise of a competition or opportunity to be chosen. It's not how the design process should work. Watch the video to hear why I think design competitions and working for free (spec work) is bad for the design industry!

DISCLAIMER: If you're a designer and you do/have decided to do projects for free and have no problem with that, I totally respect your decision! This is just my opinion after all :)

snippet.title: Design show & tell | Hand printed newspaper (Honours project)
snippet.description:
Kicking off a new series showing you some of my favourite design projects. Subscribe to my channel http://bit.ly/1aE5UOT and expand for more info!

This newspaper was made for my final Honours research project at Massey University. I focussed on looking at the way we use Twitter and the possibility of becoming "digital citizens" rather than just internet users. It's a complicated topic and I'm not sure how well I explained it in this video... so if you'd like to know more please just ask :)

The newspaper was printed using a turps transfer method and a printing press which was messy and stressful but worth it for the end result!

More about the project and the full pdf: http://charliprangley.com/portfolio/digitalcitizenship/
